companion_module.boundary_rule: The companion module preserves the no-national-net-total conclusion and does not supply a universal gallons-per-kilogram coefficient.

reasons: Resin production is classified separately from plastics and rubber product conversion.
Upstream refining, steam, electricity, hydrogen, monomers, and other chemicals can dominate indirect water but sit outside the plastics establishment.
USGS industrial data include only self-supplied withdrawals and do not report a plastics-specific consumptive-use balance.
Public-supply deliveries to industry are missing from the cited national inventory.
Life-cycle databases produce materially different water-consumption values for the same resin because of geography, allocation, technology, and co-product assumptions.
Withdrawal volume, consumption volume, water-quality impact, and water-scarcity-weighted use are different metrics.

historical_regulatory_context.combined_industries: organic chemicals, plastics, and synthetic fibers

required_method_for_plastics_policy.functional_unit: A quantified service delivered for a defined life, not one kilogram of material alone
required_method_for_plastics_policy.calculation_rule: Compute avoided product-service demand minus replacement-system impacts for each geography and scenario; never multiply national plastics tonnage by a universal gallons-per-kilogram factor.

next_data_actions: Acquire facility-level TRI/DMR, state withdrawal permits, public-utility industrial deliveries, and plant production for resin and converting facilities.
Link facilities to watersheds and seasonal stress, not only annual national totals.
Construct resin-specific and product-specific life-cycle inventories with versioned substitution assumptions.
Treat water-quality loading and thermal discharge separately from quantity consumed.
